headline: Revenue jumps on the AZEK deal, but profit margins shrink
summary_short: Revenue for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 rose 44.5% y/y to $1.40B on the AZEK acquisition, while net income fell 34.6% y/y to $28.5M as acquisition-related interest and amortization weighed on the bottom line.
summary_long: For the quarter ended March 31, 2026, revenue rose 44.5% y/y to $1.40B and gross profit rose 40.4% y/y to $523M, both lifted by the AZEK acquisition (closed July 1, 2025) remaining consolidated. Net income fell 34.6% y/y to $28.5M. The filing is James Hardie's annual 10-K for fiscal year ended March 31, 2026: full-year net sales rose 25% to $4,835.8M, but full-year net income fell 75% to $104.0M on $220.8M of incremental interest expense and AZEK purchase-accounting charges (inventory step-up, intangible amortization). Total debt rose to $4.58B and cash fell to $269M funding the deal; equity rose to $6.43B on AZEK stock consideration. For fiscal 2027, management guides capex to 6%-7% of net sales.
